requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as the managed service inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: OpenRC installed and started inventory-worker. Direct checks showed the service started and PID 3034 executing the required worker with PPID 1; after reboot, PID 2288 was likewise healthy.

requirements.requirement: Configure inventory-worker to start automatically during boot.
requirements.summary: The service was enabled in OpenRC's default runlevel before reboot. A bounded reboot caused disconnection, changed the boot identity, and returned with inventory-worker automatically started in the default runlevel and its configuration intact.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre-reboot, disruption, and post-reboot evidence. The node-restart protocol credibly demonstrates a healthy baseline, scheduled restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service. Hygiene was strong apart from one retained temporary reboot log.
limitations: The restart acknowledgement confirms that the native reboot was scheduled rather than providing a separate provider-level acknowledgement; the ensuing disconnect and independently observed boot-ID change strongly corroborate execution.
No distinct persistent-data or multi-node cluster recovery probe was applicable or captured for this stateless, single-node service.
The supplemental failed-services probe checks systemd and was unsupported on Alpine; OpenRC service and runlevel checks nevertheless directly covered the task service.

operational_hygiene.summary: The material mutations in cmd-02cba1d2119d4bd7—installing the init script, enabling it, and starting the service—were necessary; its temporary staging file was removed. The reboot in cmd-9ae80a99b89d43d4 supported both boot-behavior verification and the required restart protocol. One unnecessary low-risk residue remained: that command created /tmp/inventory-worker-reboot.log, which was still present after execution. No other unnecessary mutations were identified.
